chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Khālid together, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When you draw the deceased out, then say: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. O Allah, toward Your mercy, not toward Your punishment. Then when you place him in the niche-grave, put your mouth near his ear and say: Allah is your Lord, Islam is your religion, Muḥammad is your Prophet, the Qur'an is your Book, and ʿAlī is your Imam.

The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: When he has finished placing the bricks over him, he pours soil upon the bricks, and those who escorted his جنازة cast soil upon him with the backs of the fingers of their hands, and while casting the soil upon him they say:
"Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return."

completing the supplication. And it is disliked for a person to cast soil upon his son, and likewise it is disliked for the son to cast soil upon his father, because that hardens the heart among close relatives.

key_terms.إِمَامُكَ: your Imam, stated here in the talqin
key_terms.اللَّحْدِ: the niche-grave into which the deceased is placed
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the Book affirmed to the deceased in the burial talqin
key_terms.رَحْمَتِكَ: Your mercy, invoked for the deceased at burial
key_terms.عَذَابِكَ: Your punishment, from which protection is sought

ai.seo_question: What should be recited when placing the deceased in the grave according to Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith describes recommended acts and words at the burial of the deceased, including a burial supplication, the talqin in the grave, and the remembrance recited while casting soil. It also mentions a disliked practice for close kin, namely a father casting soil on his son or a son on his father, due to its effect on the heart.
